podcasts.title: From the Telephone to Modern Computing | James Gleick
podcasts.description:
James Gleick — acclaimed science writer and bestselling author of Chaos: Making a New Science as well as biographies on polymaths Isaac Newton and Richard Feynman — joins Sonal Chokshi and Robert Hackett to discuss his new book, The Telephone: A New History. It is a story of a device — who really invented it, how? — of a network, of a lab, and of how innovation happens.

The telephone was dismissed as a toy or a frivolity — at best, something people could use to listen to concerts or sermons from home. Even with a working invention, everyone was still trying to figure out what a telephone was for, using the framework of what they already knew. Then its users started finding their own answers. Farmers built their own decentralized networks using barbed-wire fences — the “devil’s rope” — and, over time, research at a company built around phone calls helped lay the foundations of modern computing.

This conversation explores the nuances of building at the frontier: competing inventors, the experiments, the “scenius of genius.” Why did established businesses underestimate it? Did the telephone network have to become a monopoly? What made Bell Labs so productive? 

And how a single invention could set off a technology revolution?

podcasts.title: Every Day Is Zero Day | Wiz CTO Ami Luttwak
podcasts.description:
AI isn’t just helping defenders find vulnerabilities. It’s giving attackers the speed and expertise to exploit them faster than many companies can respond. Wiz co-founder and CTO Ami Luttwak joins a16z General Partners Zane Lackey and Sarah Wang to unpack what he calls “Black October,” a wave of vulnerabilities and agentic attacks that he believes marks a turning point for cybersecurity.

They break down PHP2Shell, why AI is collapsing the time between vulnerability discovery and exploitation, and what happens when open-source models put increasingly sophisticated offensive capabilities in more hands. Ami explains why startups are becoming attractive targets, particularly when they hold valuable AI credentials, and why yesterday’s secure architecture may no longer be secure as models improve.

The conversation then turns to defense. Ami argues that companies need to continuously attack their own systems, automate investigation and patching wherever possible, design infrastructure assuming sophisticated attackers will get in, and rethink security stacks built for a slower era. His warning is simple: if attackers can move in minutes, defenders can no longer operate on human timelines.

podcasts.title: 187: 对话LiberAI刘松铭：Astra来袭，00后物理AI创始人看到的胜率
podcasts.description:
“清华、世界模型，00 后小天才”，2026 年上半年最火的投资主题。

LiberAI 创始人刘松铭完全符合这个组合。但是和他见面后，很多地方又出乎意料：

  • 他们确实刚刚发布了世界模型 Liber-0。但这也是一家起步于 2025 年年底的公司，早于英伟达 GEAR 在今年 2 月发布的 DreamZero 引起世界模型的热潮。(关于 WAM 和 DreamZero 的更多讨论，可见《晚点聊》157 期，《具身季报 26Q1》）
  • 不到一年，LiberAI 就拿了真格、红杉、龙珠、顺为等机构的 6 轮融资，但没有把公司放在中国智能最密集的五道口，而是选了北京西北角、清河站附近的一片老工业园区。这里更远、更旧、更便宜。

后来我们聊起资本纪律，刘松铭说，“就是不该花钱的地方别花钱”。

  • 创业时，刘松铭是博士三年级的学生，没有工作过、没有产业经验。但他的关注点绝不仅在技术，我们聊了很多风险管理、行业周期，以及对硬件和场景的敬畏；他也招募了一支具备 AI 算法、数据、硬件等跨领域背景的团队。
  • 大部分从研究员背景的创始人会如此描述创业的起点：想更好实现某项技术，而刘松铭说他从中学时就想创业，一直在寻找方向；技术本身不是目的，实现商业价值才是。

此时，整个物理 AI 领域的价值几何正因为 “Astra 冲击波” 被重估：即基础大模型是否会进入物理 AI 领域，完成大部分事？

刘松铭告诉我，去年底创业时，他已看到了前兆，基模可能会进入具身大脑的规划和调度层，所谓 System 2 的部分。所以 LiberAI 的核心假设就是要做全栈公司，做好与物理信息和场景相关的部分，包括精细操作能力，触觉、力觉的数据采集和训练，还有本体。

当 Astra 来袭，刘松铭分享了他看到的和选择的。

本期嘉宾：
刘松铭，LiberAI 创始人 & CEO
本期主播：
程曼祺，《晚点 LatePost》科技报道负责人

podcasts.title: Powering AI-Driven Drug Discovery with President of Isomorphic Labs Max Jaderberg
podcasts.description:
Drug discovery and development has long relied on expensive, time-consuming empirical trial and error. By shifting the discovery process onto computers, Isomorphic Labs wants to fundamentally change medicine from a process of discovery to one of precision engineering. Elad Gil sits down with Isomorphic’s president Max Jaderberg to discuss his vision for using predictive AI models to achieve experimental accuracy. Max details how the success of AlphaFold provided the first proof of concept that a deep learning model could generalize in the field of biology, and how an AI model’s compounding of learnings allows it to achieve generalizability with scale, thus greatly increasing the probability of success as well as speed in real world clinical trials. He also talks about evolving past the need for animal testing through in-silico models, Isomorphic’s focus on developing drug design engines that are agnostic of disease area, target class, and modality, why accurate molecule engineering unlocks the potential for multidrug cocktails that span complex biological pathways, and how he believes AI molecule optimization will improve both human lifespan and healthspan.

podcasts.title: The Next Era of Games: Mods, Agents, and Infinite Worlds
podcasts.description:
AI is collapsing the distance between an idea and a playable game. What happens when almost anyone can build one?

In this episode, a16z General Partners Anish Acharya and Jonathan Lai discuss how AI is changing game development, from generating art and code to operating tools like Blender and game engines directly.

They explain why cheaper development could let studios take more creative risks while opening game creation to people without traditional coding or design skills.

They also explore modding, remixing existing games, and the emergence of AI-native experiences that generate characters, abilities, and storylines on the fly, potentially creating games that never really end.
